question: Do the grid and readout effects observed in the seed-0 pilot persist across optimizer initializations (training seeds) under the identical fixed task and protocol?
scope: Same-task repetition only (same generator, distribution and sample size). Not a new task, dataset, model, loss or baseline; not evidence about other sensors, data or models.
preserved: P1-REAL-01 seed-0 pilot, its checkpoint (sha256 e4784897f5d507f0fa2bc29b2fb8d5fd7e7d81f8ad6498ce3a6f3fe9331bb455) and all its raw files are kept unchanged
ARCHITECTURE_CLAIM = STOPPED (S2); H7c_original FAIL; H7c_restated WEAK_PASS

fixed_protocol.identical_to: configs/p1_real_01.json (task, train/dev IDs 0-511 / 512-639, labels, normalization from train split, model config, Adam lr 0.003, 2000 steps, batch 32, calibration evaluation every 100 steps, lowest-calibration-MSE checkpoint with earliest step on ties including step 0)
fixed_protocol.data_identity_check: train/dev inputs and labels are generated once, sha256-hashed, cached, and their normalization statistics must equal the stored seed-0 pilot statistics exactly; every seed loads and re-verifies the same hash
fixed_protocol.eval_mode_checks: per seed: model.training is False for every submodule during calibration and test; dropout p = 0; BatchNorm uses running statistics (track_running_stats True, eval mode); every batch has equal sequence lengths (no padding, no mask); every step_scale > 0

seeds.training_seed_meaning: seed s is set in python random, numpy's global RNG and torch immediately before model construction (parameter initialization; TIDES also draws from numpy) and seeds the minibatch sampler random.Random(s); it does not touch data
seeds.data_seeds: input path of trajectory id = random.Random(1_000_000 + id); labels are deterministic RK4 of the fixed teacher
seeds.test_sampling_seed: J1 random observation times = random.Random(2_000_000 + test_id)
seeds.development_seed: seed 0 (P1-REAL-01) is the development pilot. It is (a) evaluated on the new test set as a separately marked development row and (b) retrained once with this runner only as a code-equivalence check. Neither enters the replication criterion.
seeds.replacement_runs: none; failed, diverged or timed-out seeds are reported as rows

test_set.generator: same as P1-REAL-01 (scssm.real.protocol.trajectory_path, training grid T=8, K=32, labels by ct_true with 128 RK4 sub-steps per interval, pooled label = Simpson time average)
test_set.shared_by: all seeds and the development row
test_set.generated: after this file is committed. Path seeds 1_010_000-1_010_255 and J1 seeds 2_010_000-2_010_255 are disjoint from every seed used before: FIRST_RUN 0-31, 999 and jitter-grid seeds 10_000-10_031; pilot path seeds 1_000_000-1_000_895 and pilot J1 seeds 2_000_640-2_000_895.

conditions.rule: S and H conditions keep the right-held path; J1 changes the observed path and is reported in a separate table

arms.native: the condition's grid with step_scale = dt_k / dt_train; per-step outputs read at the 32 training-grid times via the grid's base index (J1: last native output at or before each time)
arms.resampled: last observation carried forward onto the training grid using only observed times and values; step_scale = 1; on S/H this reproduces the C0 input exactly, so its zero discrepancy is an identity control, not evidence of superiority
arms.pooling_only: a readout ablation that is not part of the official model: the SAME native per-step outputs pooled by the right-endpoint time-weighted sum instead of the token mean; it is not an exact integral

definitions.yhat: per-step model output in label units
definitions.pooled_label: ybar_i = (1/T) * integral_0^T y_true_i(t) dt (Simpson on RK4 nodes of the continuous-path teacher)
definitions.p_mean: p_mean_{s,i}(c) = (1/L_c) * sum_k yhat_{s,i,k}(c) over the L_c native tokens of condition c (token mean, as TIDESClassifier's h.mean(dim=1) followed by a linear head)
definitions.p_time: p_time_{s,i}(c) = (1/T) * sum_k yhat_{s,i,k}(c) * dt_k(c) (right-endpoint time-weighted sum over the same native tokens)
definitions.p_res: p_res_{s,i}(c) = (1/K) * sum_k yhat^res_{s,i,k}(c) over the 32 resampled tokens
definitions.on_C0: the C0 grid is uniform, so p_mean(C0) = p_time(C0) = p_res(C0) =: p_{s,i}(C0)
definitions.disc: disc_{s,i}(c) = ||yhat_{s,i}(c) - yhat_{s,i}(C0)||_2 / ||yhat_{s,i}(C0)||_2 over the 32 training-grid times (final outputs, label units)
definitions.loss: L_{s,i}(arm, c) = (1/32) * sum_k (yhat_{s,i,k} - y_true_{i,k})^2 at the 32 training-grid times (label units squared)

primary.name: H8 pooled-readout effect
primary.formula: D_s = mean_i ( |p_mean_{s,i}(H8) - p_{s,i}(C0)| - |p_time_{s,i}(H8) - p_{s,i}(C0)| ), label units
primary.why_chosen: Recommended in the user instruction; this is P1-REAL-01 prediction R-P5. It was chosen AFTER seeing the seed-0 results, so it is not a blind choice.
primary.conflict_with_existing_protocol: P1-REAL-01 did not designate a single primary estimand (it had four predictions R-P1..R-P5). The superseded, never-run NX1 draft named splitting consistency at m=8 as primary; that quantity is kept here as the first secondary estimand rather than silently dropped.

secondary.S8_discrepancy: mean_i disc_{s,i}(S8) in float32; precision diagnostic: the same computed with weights and inputs cast to float64
secondary.loss_contrast: r_s(c) = (mean_i L_{s,i}(native,c) - mean_i L_{s,i}(resampled,c)) / mean_i L_{s,i}(resampled,c) for c in S2,S4,S8,H8 (and J1 in the secondary table); absolute difference also reported
secondary.pooled_error: mean_i |p_arm_{s,i}(c) - ybar_i| for each arm and c in C0,S8,H8,J1; E_s = mean_i (|p_mean(H8) - ybar| - |p_time(H8) - ybar|)
secondary.cost: end-to-end and forward-only wall time and process CPU time per condition batch

statistics.design: seed x trajectory is a crossed design (all seeds share the same 256 test trajectories); the 4 x 256 values are NOT treated as iid
statistics.within_seed_uncertainty: paired percentile bootstrap over test trajectories with the seed fixed (2000 draws, seed 0; the same trajectory draws are reused for every estimand and seed); ratios are recomputed with numerator and denominator in every draw
statistics.across_seeds: the four per-seed estimates are reported individually with their min, max and mean; no pooled CI and no claim about the population of training runs
statistics.margin_rule_for_r: 'no practical difference' only if the 95% CI of r_s lies inside (-0.05, +0.05); 'native lower/higher' if the CI excludes 0 on one side, with 'beyond margin' only if it also excludes the margin; otherwise inconclusive. The 5% is a convention (about 2.5% in RMSE), not an application-derived tolerance; a non-significant difference is never read as equivalence.
statistics.small_denominator: if mean_i L_resampled < 1e-12, r_s is NA and only the absolute difference is reported
statistics.exploratory_previous_analysis: the P1-REAL-01 fixed-estimated-margin analysis (margin = 5% of the point-estimated resampled MSE) is kept as an exploratory seed-0 result; the seed-0 pilot is additionally re-summarized from its raw with the r_s estimator as a derived file, clearly marked as the old test set

replication_criterion.primary: the H8 pooled-readout effect is called replicated within this task if D_s > 0 with the 95% CI excluding 0 for every seed s in {1,2,3,4}; otherwise it is reported as not replicated or unstable, as observed
replication_criterion.secondary_S8: the S8 discrepancy is called above the float32 floor for a seed if its CI lower bound exceeds 1e-4

timing_protocol.batch: all 256 test sequences of one condition in one batch
timing_protocol.end_to_end_boundary: from the list of observed grids (times, values) to per-step predictions at the 32 training-grid times, including LOCF resampling (resampled arm), tensor construction, forward, de-normalization and readout mapping
timing_protocol.reported: median and min wall seconds (time.perf_counter) and median process CPU seconds (time.process_time, summed over threads) per condition, arm and seed; tokens per sequence; batch size; threads. Timed repeats are not independent performance samples.
timing_protocol.cost_ratio_naming: ratios are written as numerator/denominator with both names, e.g. native_S8_end_to_end / resampled_S8_end_to_end

additional_diagnostics.layer_precision: the stored seed-0 layer diagnostic is reused; a per-seed layer diagnostic is run only if some training seed has mean S8 discrepancy below 1e-3 (within 10x of the float32 floor)
additional_diagnostics.equivalence_check: retrain seed 0 with this runner and compare every tensor of the selected state with the frozen pilot checkpoint (expected exactly equal); an engineering check, reported separately

outputs.files: data_cache.json + data_hash.json, testset_cache.json, seed{s}/train.json, seed{s}/train.log, seed{s}/checkpoint.pt (not exported), seed{s}/eval.jsonl, seed{s}/eval_summary.json, eqcheck.json, aggregate.json
